card.name: temporary_and_ccz_lowering
card.precondition: family = dv_recon (Toffoli-level op list, no continuous Rz); op list contains at least one ccz (or ccx, which is h-ccz-h on the target); total qubits <= 20 so the whole-circuit check still runs; at least one clean |0> ancilla can be appended (here 11 -> 12 qubits, or 11 -> 11+k if k AND gadgets must be live at once).
card.identity: Replace each CCZ(c1,c2,t) by: (1) Gidney temporary-AND compute |c1,c2,0> -> |c1,c2, c1&c2> on a fresh clean ancilla a, using the 4-T gadget (H(a); T(a); CX(c1,a); CX(c2,a); CX(a,b-free form) ... concretely the standard circuit H a, T a, CX c1 a, CX c2 a, CX a x with T^dag on the two control legs and T on a, S, H a-free Clifford frame: exactly 4 T / T^dag and the rest Clifford); (2) CZ(a,t) -- Clifford, 0 T; (3) measurement-based uncompute of a: H(a), measure a in the computational basis giving m, and apply CZ(c1,c2) classically conditioned on m=1, then discard a -- 0 T. Net 4 T per CCZ instead of 7. SECOND CLAUSE (the pair merge): if two CCZs share the same unordered control pair {c1,c2} and no op between them acts on c1 or c2, compute the AND once, apply CZ(a,t1) and CZ(a,t2), and uncompute once -- 4 T for the two gates together instead of 14. The same holds for a run of k such CCZs.
card.correctness: Gidney's gadget implements the isometry |c1,c2>|0> -> |c1,c2>|c1 AND c2> exactly over Z[omega] (it is Clifford+T with 4 T, verifiable by the exact D[omega] check on the 3-qubit block). Since CCZ is diagonal, CCZ(c1,c2,t) = CZ(a,t) conditioned on a = c1&c2: on basis state |c1,c2,t> the phase applied is (-1)^{(c1&c2)·t}, which is exactly CCZ's phase. Uncompute: after the CZ the ancilla is still |c1&c2> (CZ is diagonal and does not disturb it), so H then a computational-basis measurement is an X-basis measurement of |c1&c2>, outcome m uniform and independent of the data; the post-measurement data state is (-1)^{m(c1&c2)} times the correct state, i.e. the residual operator is CZ(c1,c2)^m, undone exactly by the classically controlled CZ(c1,c2). Each branch therefore applies K_m = (correct unitary) with c_m = 1/sqrt(2) for both m -- the same constant for every input x, so invariant 2 (phase consistency) holds and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. Ancilla returns to a measured-and-discarded state, replaced by a fresh |0> for the next gadget. Pair-merge clause: if no op between the two CCZs touches c1 or c2, the ancilla register still holds c1&c2 at the second CCZ, so the single AND is valid for both; the intervening ops commute with the (identity) action on a.
card.trigger: Scan the op list for ops of type ccz (and ccx, read as h(t)-ccz-h(t)). Each such op fires clause 1 unconditionally. Clause 2 fires on a maximal run ccz(c1,c2,t_1), ..., ccz(c1,c2,t_k) with the SAME unordered control pair {c1,c2} such that every op strictly between consecutive members of the run has empty qubit intersection with {c1,c2}; the run is then lowered with one AND compute and one measured uncompute. Ancilla allocation: a single ancilla suffices if gadgets never nest (lower them in circuit order, releasing a after each uncompute); allocate a second only if a run's span overlaps another run's span.
card.expected_effect: The 17 CCZ gates are the entire non-Clifford content (119 T = 17 x 7). Clause 1 alone makes every CCZ cost 4 T: 17 x 4 = 68 T, i.e. -51 T, already below pyzx's 73. Clause 2: the fingerprint reports 7 shared_control_pairs; each run of two that survives the no-intervening-touch test removes a further 4 T, so if all 7 fire the circuit reaches (17-7) x 4 = 40 T, -79. The 30 H, 24 X and 3 CX are untouched (the gadget adds only Clifford H/S/CX plus one classically controlled CZ per gadget). Cost: +1 clean ancilla (11 -> 12 qubits), 10-17 mid-circuit measurements with feed-forward, zero error drawn.
card.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), arXiv:1709.06648 -- the temporary-AND gadget (4 T compute, measurement-based 0 T uncompute); the CCZ = AND + CZ + uncompute factorization is the standard AutoCCZ/CCZ-from-AND form used in Gidney-Ekera (arXiv:1905.09749).

card.name: ccz_catalyzed_two_t_lowering
card.precondition: Toffoli-level IRCircuit (family dv_recon) containing at least one ccz or ccx (h-ccx-h counts), ancilla_room >= 2 clean qubits, measurement and classically controlled Cliffords permitted; no bound on how the controls are shared (unlike the run-sharing AND rule, each ccz is lowered on its own). 3 <= qubits <= 20.
card.identity: Gidney-Jones CCZ-to-2T catalysis. Keep ONE persistent catalyst qubit c in the magic state |T> = T|+> = (|0> + e^{i pi/4}|1>)/sqrt(2), prepared once with a single T gate on |+>. Each ccz(x,y,z) is then replaced by a gadget of Cliffords + exactly 2 T gates + 1 fresh clean ancilla a + one mid-circuit measurement of a (X basis) + classically controlled Cliffords, at the end of which a is returned to |0> and c is returned to |T>. Structurally: the standard 4-T AND/CCZ gadget phases three CX-parities of (x,y,a) by T/T/Tdg; with the catalyst present, two of those T phases are not paid for but TELEPORTED out of c by a Clifford circuit (CX/CZ between c and the parity wire plus a measurement and a classically controlled S/Z/CZ fix-up) which consumes and immediately re-prepares |T> on c, leaving only 2 T gates to be paid. n ccz gates therefore cost 2n + 1 T instead of 7n (or 4n with the plain AND gadget), the +1 being the one-time catalyst preparation. The catalyst is threaded through the whole circuit in topological order so all 16 gadgets reuse the same c; the single fresh ancilla a is likewise reused because the gadgets are applied one at a time and a is restored to |0> before the next one.
card.correctness: CCZ is the diagonal unitary |x,y,z> -> (-1)^{xyz}|x,y,z>, and xyz as a phase polynomial over F2 is a signed sum of T-phases on CX-parities: 8*xyz = (x+y+z) - (x^y) - (y^z) - (x^z) + (x^y^z) mod 2 arithmetic lifted to Z8, which is the usual 7-T Clifford+T decomposition; routing the pair (x,y) through a clean ancilla a with a = x AND y gives the 4-T gadget, whose uncompute is an X-basis measurement of a with a classically controlled CZ(x,y) and so costs 0 T. The catalysis step is the exact gate-teleportation identity of Gidney & Jones: for the Clifford circuit C on (c, p) with c in |T>, measuring the designated output wire and applying the Clifford fix-up conditioned on the outcome implements T on the parity wire p and returns c to |T> exactly, on every branch and with the SAME amplitude on every branch, because |T> is a +1 eigenstate-up-to-Clifford resource (T^2 = S is Clifford, so the two measurement branches differ only by a Clifford that the fix-up removes). Hence the construction is exact (zero error, no budget drawn), and it satisfies the specification contract of invariant 2: the fresh ancilla starts and ends in |0>, the catalyst starts and ends in |T>, and each measurement branch applies K_m = c_m * CCZ with the same c_m for all inputs. The judge's branch-wise specification check sees the composition as a unitary on (data + catalyst) once the catalyst is included in the window.
card.trigger: Scan the op list for every gate named ccz, or ccx (and the pattern h(t) ccz h(t) which is a ccx). Fire when at least one such gate exists AND the circuit has room for 2 appended ancillas (append_ancillas(c, 2): one catalyst, one AND workspace). One match per ccz/ccx gate, emitted in op order so that the catalyst wire is threaded sequentially; the first match also emits the one-time h + t preparation of the catalyst and the last match leaves it in place (it is a returned resource, not garbage). Does not require shared_control_pairs > 0, which is why it fires on mult_4 where the run-sharing AND rule has nothing to merge.
card.expected_effect: All 16 ccz gates on mult_4 stop costing 7 T each. 16 * 2 = 32 T for the gadgets plus 1 T for the single catalyst preparation = 33 T; the 14 h and 3 cx are untouched and contribute no T. Qubits go 12 -> 14, CNOT count rises by roughly 6-8 per gadget (~100 extra CX, Clifford and therefore free in this cost model, and lexicographically only the third key). Final T 33 against the current 112 and against pyzx's 68, i.e. it also clears the best baseline by about half. Conservative floor if two or three gadgets are rejected and fall back to the 4-T AND form: ~40 T.
card.source: C. Gidney and C. Jones, 'A CCZ to 2T transformation', Quantum 3, 135 (2019) [arXiv:1812.01238]; catalyst/magic-state-reuse framing in Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition' (2018); underlying 4-T measured AND gadget from C. Jones, 'Low-overhead constructions for the fault-tolerant Toffoli gate', Phys. Rev. A 87, 022328 (2013).

card.name: carry_chain_recognition_ripple_resynthesis
card.precondition: family dv_recon; Toffoli-level op list whose gates are only x / cx / cz / h / ccx / ccz / and_compute / and_uncompute / measure (no rz, no off-grid rotation), every cz or ccz reducible to cx/ccx by the h immediately before and after on its target wire, 10 <= qubits <= 34, ancilla_room available. Circuits with any gate outside this classical-reversible class are excluded and cost nothing.
card.identity: Recognize the whole op list as the in-place binary adder permutation |a>|b>|0...0> -> |a>|a+b mod 2^n>|0...0> (optionally with one carry-out wire holding bit n), then replace the ENTIRE circuit by Gidney's temporary-AND ripple-carry adder for the same wire assignment. Carry recurrence: c_0 = 0, c_{i+1} = a_i b_i XOR c_i (a_i XOR b_i) = MAJ(a_i, b_i, c_i), s_i = a_i XOR b_i XOR c_i. Per bit i, forward sweep: cx(a_i, b_i); cx(a_i, c_i); and_compute(b_i, c_i -> w_i) [4 T]; cx(w_i, a_i) so a_i now carries c_{i+1}; use a_i as the next carry wire. Backward sweep: for each i in reverse, and_uncompute(w_i) [0 T, measure w_i in the X basis and apply the classically controlled cz fix-up], then undo the linear wrapping with cx's and write s_i into b_i. The n-1 (or n) AND gadgets are the only non-Clifford content; the lookahead circuit's ~57 Toffolis, which recompute generate/propagate products across a logarithmic-depth tree, are discarded entirely.
card.correctness: The target is a permutation of computational basis states with no relative phase (every gate in the precondition class is a signed classical-reversible gate once cz/ccz are rewritten to cx/ccx by their flanking Hadamards, and and_compute/and_uncompute form an exact unitary pair on a clean ancilla). For n = 8 the data register is 16 bits, so the trigger CERTIFIES the permutation exhaustively: simulate all 2^16 assignments of (a, b) with all ancillas at 0 and require output = (a, a + b mod 2^n) (plus carry-out if a wire for it is identified) and every ancilla back at 0. Equality of two classical-reversible circuits on every basis state, with ancillas restored on every one of them, is equality of unitaries up to global phase - there is no phase freedom left to check because the class has none. Gidney's gadget is itself exact: and_compute(x,y->w) leaves w = xy, and the measurement-based uncompute is the identity on the data for both measurement branches once the classically controlled cz fix-up is applied, so invariant 2 (same c_m for every input, sum |c_m|^2 = 1) holds branch-wise. The carry recurrence above is the standard MAJ/UMA ripple-carry identity, verified bit by bit.
card.trigger: Fires at most once, on the whole op list. (1) All gates in the precondition class and every cz/ccz resolves to cx/ccx; else decline. (2) Partition the wires into candidate registers by the exhaustive classical simulation: find a pair of n-bit index tuples (A, B) and a set Z of ancilla wires such that for all 2^(2n) inputs the induced map is (a, b) -> (a, a+b mod 2^n) on (A, B) with Z restored to 0; search A, B over the natural adder layouts (wires that are never written vs. wires whose output bit depends on all lower a_j, b_j), not over all tuples. (3) If such (A, B, Z) exists, emit one match carrying the wire assignment; the apply step rebuilds the circuit from scratch as the ripple-carry cascade on those exact wires, allocating n-1 clean ancillas with append_ancillas if fewer than n-1 wires of Z are free. If no assignment validates, emit nothing.
card.expected_effect: All 54 and_compute gadgets, all 54 and_uncompute gadgets and the 57 cz / 67 cx of the lookahead tree are deleted and replaced by 7-8 and_compute / and_uncompute pairs plus ~40 cx and a few x gates. Non-Clifford cost goes from 54 x 4 T = 216 T to 8 x 4 T = 32 T (7 ANDs = 28 T if the top carry-out wire is not used, so the circuit is mod 2^8). This also lands well under pyzx's 173, which cannot reach it because full_reduce preserves the lookahead's Toffoli count structure and never trades depth for T. Qubit count stays at or below 25 (the lookahead's tree ancillas are freed; at most n-1 = 7 are needed live). CNOT count falls as well, so the lexicographic cost order improves on all three entries. Depth grows from O(log n) to O(n), which the cost order does not price.
card.source: Craig Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) - temporary AND / measurement-based uncompute giving 4n T per n-bit addition; Cuccaro, Draper, Kutin, Moulton, 'A new quantum ripple-carry addition circuit', quant-ph/0410184 (the MAJ/UMA carry recurrence); contrast with Draper, Kutin, Rains, Svore, 'A logarithmic-depth quantum carry-lookahead adder', quant-ph/0406142, which is the structure the input implements.

card.name: separated_toffoli_pair_temporary_and_sharing
card.precondition: dv_recon / Toffoli-level IRCircuit: needs toffoli (ccz or ccx present), needs ancilla_room, measurement allowed; qubits <= 24. Requires at least two ccz/ccx gates that share a control pair (shared_control_pairs > 0). No rotations required.
card.identity: Let g_i = CCZ(x,y,z) at position i and g_j = CCZ(x,y,z') at a LATER position j (for ccx, z/z' is the target; for ccz pick any wire as the 'target' and the other two as the AND pair), with the SAME unordered pair {x,y} as AND pair. Suppose no gate strictly between i and j writes x or y (x,y may be read as controls, i.e. appear as a control of cx/cz/ccz, but never as a cx/ccx target, x, h, or measurement target). Then the value a = x AND y is constant over the whole span [i, j]. Rewrite: insert and_compute(x, y -> a) on a fresh clean ancilla a immediately before position i (4 T), replace g_i by cz(a, z) (or cx(a, z) for ccx), leave every op in between untouched, replace g_j by cz(a, z') (resp. cx(a, z')), and insert and_uncompute(a) immediately after position j (0 T: measure a in the X basis, classically controlled cz(x,y) fix-up). Cost: 4 T for the pair instead of 7 + 7 = 14 T. The construction generalises to a chain of k same-AND-pair gates in the span, giving 4 T for all k instead of 7k. Spans are processed greedily longest-first; overlapping spans with different AND pairs each get their own ancilla (ancillas are reused once their span closes), nested spans are allowed.
card.correctness: CCZ(x,y,z) = CZ(a,z) and CCX(x,y;z) = CX(a;z) whenever the ancilla a holds the Boolean x AND y, on every computational basis state, with no phase: both are diagonal/permutation operators whose action depends only on the product x*y. Gidney's temporary-AND gadget (arXiv:1709.06648) computes a = x AND y on a clean |0> ancilla with 4 T and T-depth 1, and uncomputes it with zero T by measuring the ancilla in the X basis and applying a classically controlled CZ(x,y) to clear the measurement-induced phase kickback; the uncompute is exact, restores a to |0>, and is correct for ARBITRARY superpositions of x,y because the correction is itself controlled on x,y. The only hypothesis needed is that x and y are unwritten on the span, which makes a = x AND y an invariant there; the intervening ops may freely read x, y, and read or write z, because each original gate is replaced in place by an equivalent two-qubit gate at exactly its own position, so the operator ordering of the whole circuit is unchanged. The accepted rule and_ancilla_ccz_lowering_with_measured_uncompute is the special case where the gates are ADJACENT (a run); this is why it leaves adder_6 at 11 x 7 = 77 T. The relaxation 'controls unwritten' rather than 'nothing in between' is the whole content of the idea, and it is exactly the compute/uncompute structure of a ripple-carry adder: the carry Toffoli and its mirror image share the same control pair, and only the carry wire is touched in between.
card.trigger: Scan the op list for ccz/ccx gates. Group them by unordered AND-pair candidate: for ccx take {controls}; for ccz take all three 2-subsets of its wires. For each candidate pair {x,y} and each pair of occurrences i < j in its occurrence list, accept the span if (a) no op in (i, j) has x or y as a WRITTEN qubit - written = cx/ccx target, x, h, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz, measure, or either wire of a non-diagonal gate - and (b) a clean ancilla is available (append_ancillas). Emit one match per maximal such span, with the list of member gate positions, preferring the span covering the most ccz/ccx gates; matches are emitted in order of decreasing member count and the runner applies them one at a time, re-triggering after each.
card.expected_effect: adder_6 has 11 ccz and fingerprint reports 5 shared_control_pairs, i.e. 5 compute/uncompute carry pairs plus one unpaired ccz. Each qualifying pair falls from 14 T to 4 T. If all 5 pairs qualify: 5*4 + 7 = 27 T (saving 50). Conservatively assuming 4 of the 5 spans survive the 'controls unwritten' test and the remaining 3 ccz stay at 7 T: 4*4 + 21 = 37 T (saving 40). Qubits rise by the number of simultaneously open spans (at most 5, so 14 -> at most 19) and CNOT count rises slightly, but cost order is lexicographic in (T, qubits, CNOT), so the T drop decides. This also crosses the best baseline, pyzx at 47, which is unitary-only and cannot use measurement.

card.name: dyadic_rz_phase_gradient_catalysis
card.precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz and ancilla_room; min_qubits 2, max_qubits 20. Fires only if at least 8 non-Clifford rz angles are exact multiples of pi/2^m for some m <= 8 (|theta - k*pi/2^m| <= 1e-12 via v4.api.angles.dyadic). qft_8 satisfies this maximally: fingerprint exactly_dyadic[8] = 33 of 33 off-grid rotations.
card.identity: Prepare ONE catalyst register of M = 9 qubits in the phase-gradient state |g> = 2^(-M/2) sum_y e^(-2*pi*i*y/2^M)|y>, i.e. one Rz(-2*pi/2^j) (= one rotation of angle 2*pi/2^j) on each gradient bit j = 1..M after Hadamards; j = 1,2,3 are Clifford/T, only j = 4..9 need gridsynth, and they are paid ONCE for the whole circuit. Then replace every rotation rz(theta) with theta = k*pi/2^m (m <= 8, k odd) on qubit q by: a q-controlled addition of the CLASSICAL constant c = k * 2^(M-m-1) into the gradient register mod 2^M, built from m and_compute gadgets (4 T each) on one clean carry ancilla, m cx/x fix-ups, and m measurement-based and_uncompute (0 T). The gradient register comes out in |g> again (catalysis: it is restored, not consumed, so all 33 rotations share one preparation), the carry ancilla returns to |0>, and no rotation on the data qubits remains for gridsynth to synthesize. This is NOT in the floor tier of this book (BOOK.md floor = dpf_dyadic_angle_fixing + the two pyzx-class Pauli merges only); it differs from a register-register adder construction in that each rotation becomes a CONSTANT addition, whose trailing M-m-1 zero bits are free, so the cost is 4m T and not 4M T.
card.correctness: Adding c mod 2^M to |g> gives 2^(-M/2) sum_y e^(-2*pi*i*y/2^M)|y+c> = e^(+2*pi*i*c/2^M) |g> by reindexing z = y+c (the sum is cyclic, so mod-2^M addition is exactly the shift that reproduces the state). The adder is therefore a unitary that multiplies by the scalar e^(2*pi*i*c/2^M) and leaves the register invariant. Controlling it on q puts that scalar only on the |1>_q branch, i.e. diag(1, e^(2*pi*i*c/2^M)) on q = Rz(2*pi*c/2^(M-1)) up to global phase; with c = k*2^(M-m-1) this is exactly Rz(k*pi/2^m) = the deleted gate. Since the gate is diagonal in the computational basis of q, the substitution is valid at any position in the op list, Hadamards included. The and_compute/and_uncompute gadgets are Gidney's temporary AND: exact, and the uncompute is an X-basis measurement with a classically controlled CZ fix-up, so the ancilla is deterministically returned to |0> on every branch and the Kraus operator of every measurement branch is the same unitary up to the same phase (invariant 2 holds branch-wise). The only error is the finite-precision synthesis of the 6 gradient-preparation rotations; the whole-circuit judge measures the phase-aligned distance of the result against the ORIGINAL circuit, which is what the drawn budget covers.
card.trigger: Scan the op list for ops with rotation(op) not None and not on_grid(theta); for each, let d = angles.nearest(theta, kmax=8) and keep the match if d.distance == 0 (exact dyadic) and 3 <= d.m <= 8. Emit one match per such rotation, plus a single circuit-level match that appends the M = 9 gradient qubits and 1 carry ancilla (append_ancillas) and emits the preparation prefix / its inverse suffix. If fewer than 8 rotation matches survive, emit nothing (the one-time preparation cost cannot be amortized).
card.expected_effect: All 33 off-grid rz on the 8 data qubits disappear, so gridsynth pays for 0 of them instead of 33 at eps_rz = 3.03e-5 (~45 T each, which is essentially the whole current 1583). They are replaced by 4m T of exact AND gadgets each: by the fingerprint's level histogram (8 rotations at m=3, 7 at m=4, 6 at m=5, 5 at m=6, 4 at m=7, 3 at m=8) that is 8*12 + 7*16 + 6*20 + 5*24 + 4*28 + 3*32 = 656 T, plus ~270 T for the 6 off-grid gradient-preparation rotations synthesized once at eps ~2.5e-5 (0.00015 drawn, split 6 ways), plus the 11 explicit t/tdg that stay. Scored conservatively against the current 1583 in case the carry ancilla needs a second qubit and the preparation is charged at full eps_rz.

card.name: qft_ladder_register_add_into_catalytic_phase_gradient
card.precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz and ancilla_room; 4 <= qubits <= 13. Requires at least one Hadamard-free segment containing >= 4 non-Clifford rz whose angles are EXACTLY dyadic (k*pi/2^m, k odd, m >= 3) and whose front-frame axes are weight-1 Z on DISTINCT qubits with consecutive levels m, m+1, ..., m+r (geometric halving). qae_13's angle histogram is exactly this triangle (pi/8 x11, pi/16 x10, pi/32 x9, ..., pi/4096 x2, plus the pi/2-pi/2^m family = S-dag times the same ladder), so the trigger is the inverse-QFT ladder of the counting register.
card.identity: Let a maximal ladder be rotations Rz(s*2pi/2^{j+1}) on distinct qubits q_0..q_{K-1}, s = +-1, i.e. the diagonal map |y> -> e^{i*s*2pi*y/2^K}|y> where y = sum_j 2^j x_{q_j} is the register value read in the ladder's own bit order. Allocate ONE K-qubit catalyst register in the phase-gradient state |grad_K> = 2^{-K/2} sum_g e^{2pi i g/2^K}|g> (prepared once per circuit by K single-qubit rz(2pi/2^{j+1}) on |+>^K, and restored unchanged by every use, so no uncompute and no per-use prep). Replace the whole ladder by ONE K-bit in-place addition |y>|g> -> |y>|g - s*y mod 2^K> implemented with Gidney temporary-AND adders (and_compute 4 T, measurement-based and_uncompute 0 T, classically controlled fix-ups), using 1 extra clean ancilla for the carry. Partial ladders (a sub-triangle of levels) use a K' = (number of levels present) wide window of the same shared gradient register; a ladder whose angles are k*pi/2^m with k odd and not a power-of-two multiple is first split into its binary digits, each digit landing on a different gradient bit of the SAME addition.
card.correctness: Phase kickback into the gradient (Kitaev; Gidney 2018). ADD_{-s*y}|grad_K> = 2^{-K/2} sum_g e^{2pi i g/2^K}|g - s*y> = e^{i*s*2pi*y/2^K} * 2^{-K/2} sum_{g'} e^{2pi i g'/2^K}|g'> = e^{i*s*2pi*y/2^K}|grad_K>. So the data register acquires exactly the ladder's diagonal phase on every computational basis state and the catalyst comes out in |grad_K> exactly (it is a catalyst, not an ancilla that must be uncomputed). The identity is exact in Z[omega] up to the synthesis of the K prep rotations, which are ordinary off-grid rz charged to final synthesis as always. The Gidney adder is exact and measurement-based: for each measurement branch m the applied Kraus operator is K_m|x> = c_m|f(x)>, the classically controlled fix-ups make c_m branch-independent, and the AND ancillas return to |0>, so invariant 2 holds branch-wise. Mod-2^K wraparound is harmless: the phase is e^{2pi i (.) /2^K}, periodic mod 2^K.
card.trigger: For each Hadamard-free segment (api.dv.segments) take api.pauli.frames / api.phasepoly.rotation_labels; keep rotations whose axis is weight-1 Z and whose angle satisfies api.angles.nearest(theta, kmax=14) with distance 0 and m >= 3. card.name: anf_polynomial_toffoli_cancellation
card.precondition: family = dv_recon (Toffoli-level IRCircuit, zero continuous Rz, measurement-free input); needs toffoli; qubits <= 20 so the whole-circuit judge still runs; the op list must contain at least one maximal classical-reversible segment, i.e. a contiguous run of ops drawn only from {x, cx, ccx, ccz, and h(q) pairs that sandwich a ccz on q and so read as ccx} containing >= 2 ccx/ccz, with no s/sdg/t/tdg and no unpaired h inside it. No ancillas, no measurement, no error drawn.
card.identity: Inside one classical-reversible segment, propagate the exact GF(2) algebraic normal form (ANF) of each wire. Initialise p_q = x_q (the segment's input variables). Then x(q): p_q ^= 1; cx(a,b): p_b ^= p_a; ccx(a,b -> t): p_t ^= p_a * p_b (polynomial product in GF(2)[x], squarefree-reduced by x^2 = x); ccz(a,b,c) is read as h(c) ccx(a,b -> c) h(c) wherever the sandwiching h's are present, otherwise left alone. Three rewrites, each applied to a single op and each exact: (R1) DEGENERATE CONTROL - if the ANF of p_a (or p_b) at that op's position is the constant 0, delete the ccx entirely; if it is the constant 1, replace ccx(a,b -> t) by cx(b,t) (resp. cx(a,t)). (R2) IDEMPOTENT CANCELLATION - if the monomial set of the product p_a * p_b is already a subset of the monomial set of p_t that was written by an EARLIER ccx(a',b' -> t) in the same segment with p_{a'} * p_{b'} == p_a * p_b (equal ANFs), and no op between the two writes any of the variables occurring in p_a, p_b, then both ccx ops are deleted and replaced by nothing: the two identical product terms XOR to 0. The intervening ops are unchanged because they never read t (checked) or read t only through further products that are recomputed from the restored ANF. (R3) LINEARISED PRODUCT - if p_a * p_b reduces, after squarefree reduction, to a polynomial of degree <= 1 (e.g. p_a == p_b, giving p_a * p_a = p_a, or p_a = 1 ^ p_b), replace the ccx by the equivalent Clifford net: a cx ladder realising p_t ^= (that affine form), i.e. cx's from the form's support plus one x if its constant is 1. Each fired rewrite removes one Toffoli, i.e. 7 T, and adds only x/cx/cz (0 T).
card.correctness: A segment of x/cx/ccx is a classical reversible map; its action on a computational basis state is exactly the simultaneous substitution of the per-wire ANFs, which is why propagating the ANF is a faithful (not approximate) symbolic execution of the segment. GF(2) arithmetic gives the three facts used: (i) 0 * p = 0 and 1 * p = p, so a control whose ANF is constant makes the Toffoli either the identity or a CNOT (R1); (ii) u ^ u = 0, so writing the same product twice into the same wire leaves it unchanged - deleting both writes yields the identical substitution map, hence the identical permutation unitary (R2), with the no-intervening-write side condition ensuring p_a, p_b have the same ANF at both positions; (iii) p * p = p over GF(2) under x^2 = x, and (1 ^ p) * p = p ^ p = 0, so products of dependent controls collapse to affine forms realisable by CNOT/X (R3). Because the segment is a permutation of basis states with no phases, equality of the substitution maps implies equality of the unitaries exactly - no global or relative phase is introduced, so invariants 1, 2 and 6 all hold and the frozen judge's exact D[omega] check on the changed window applies with zero ledger charge. The h(c)-ccz-h(c) reading is the standard CCX = H_t CCZ H_t identity, exact over Z[omega]; a ccz whose target is not H-sandwiched is simply not matched.
card.trigger: Walk the op list, cutting segments at any t/tdg/s/sdg, any measurement, and any h that is not the first or second member of an h(q) ... h(q) pair enclosing a ccz acting on q with no other op touching q in between. Matches are emitted in circuit order and re-propagated after each accepted application, so a cancellation that makes a later control constant is found on the next pass. ANF size is capped (refuse the segment if any wire's monomial set exceeds 4096 terms) so the pass is bounded.

card.name: bilinear_and_complexity_karatsuba_resynthesis
card.precondition: Toffoli-level IRCircuit, family dv_recon, measurement-free input, gate names drawn only from {ccz, ccx, cx, x, h} (h appearing only as the pair h(t) ... h(t) that turns a ccz into a ccx on wire t, i.e. the circuit is a reversible XOR-AND network with no non-Clifford rotations), at least 4 ccz/ccx gates, every ccz/ccx control pair distinct from its target wire, ancilla_room >= 6 clean qubits, 6 <= qubits <= 20. Circuits with rotations, with measurements already present, or whose AND terms do not form a bilinear map over two disjoint input registers are excluded by the declared check and cost nothing.
card.identity: Bilinear-form resynthesis (Karatsuba / subquadratic F_2^n multiplication, Kepley-Steinwandt). Read the network as a map: sweep the op list with affine parity labels (v4.api.phasepoly.labels) so each wire carries a parity p = (mask, const) of the input qubits; each ccz/ccx then contributes one AND term p_c1 AND p_c2 XORed into its target wire. Collect, per output wire k, the F2 bilinear form B_k(a,b) = XOR over a set S_k of products a_i b_j, where the input qubits split into two disjoint registers A = {a_0..a_{r-1}} and B = {b_0..b_{s-1}} (the split is read off the label masks: every AND term has one control whose mask lies in A and one in B; if not, decline). The 16 terms of mult_4 are exactly the products a_i b_j of two 4-bit registers, reduced into 4+ output wires by the field polynomial. Replace the whole collection of AND gates by a bilinear decomposition of rank m < |union of S_k|: a list of m triples (u_t, w_t, c_t) with u_t a subset of A, w_t a subset of B, such that for every k, B_k = XOR over t in T_k of (XOR_{i in u_t} a_i)(XOR_{j in w_t} b_j). For a 4x4 register this is two-level Karatsuba, m = 9: split a = a_hi x^2 + a_lo, b likewise, use the 3 products (a_lo b_lo), (a_hi b_hi), ((a_lo+a_hi)(b_lo+b_hi)) at the top level and the same 3-product trick inside each 2x2 product. Emission: (1) form each needed sum with CNOTs in place on a scratch wire (cx from each i in u_t onto a fresh clean ancilla, same for w_t), (2) one ccx computing the product onto a fresh clean product ancilla, (3) cx each product ancilla into every output wire k with t in T_k, (4) uncompute every scratch and product ancilla by replaying step (2) and step (1) in reverse, returning them to |0>. Scratch wires are reused across the m products, so the extra qubit count is bounded by 2 scratch + 1 product-accumulator live at a time plus the ancillas needed to hold products whose consumers come later; with the Karatsuba schedule 6 clean ancillas suffice for r = s = 4. The original ccz/ccx gates and their h conjugations are deleted.
card.correctness: Over F2 the AND/XOR network computes a polynomial map, and because A and B are disjoint input registers each output is a bilinear form B_k(a,b) = a^T M_k b with M_k the 0/1 incidence matrix of S_k. Bilinear decomposition is the statement M_k = XOR_{t in T_k} u_t w_t^T, i.e. the matrices M_k lie in the F2 span of the m rank-one matrices u_t w_t^T; the Karatsuba identity (a_lo + a_hi)(b_lo + b_hi) = a_lo b_lo + a_lo b_hi + a_hi b_lo + a_hi b_hi over F2 (characteristic 2, so no sign bookkeeping and no subtraction) supplies such a decomposition with m = 9 for r = s = 4, and recursively m = 3^ceil(log2 r) in general. Each product (XOR u_t)(XOR w_t) is computed by a single Toffoli onto a clean |0> ancilla, which is exactly its truth table; XORing it into the output wires is a CNOT, which adds the term mod 2; replaying the Toffoli and the sum-forming CNOTs in reverse order restores the ancillas to |0> because every gate used is its own inverse and acts on wires whose values at that point are unchanged (the controls are untouched between compute and uncompute, as the schedule interleaves nothing that writes to A or B). Hence the rewrite is exact up to nothing at all: the same permutation on the data wires, ancillas |0> -> |0>, no measurement, no phase to reconcile, so error_class exact and zero draw from the ledger. The judge sees a unitary-to-unitary Clifford+T rewrite on the changed window and can certify it exactly in D[omega]; the branch-wise specification check is trivial since there are no branches. The decomposition itself is verified structurally before emission by recomputing the incidence matrices M_k from the proposed triples and comparing to the extracted ones over F2, so an incorrect decomposition is never emitted.
card.trigger: Fire once per circuit (one match, a whole-network substitution, not a local template). Compute parity labels over the op list; require that every ccz/ccx has its two controls labelled by masks that are nonzero and lie in two disjoint input-register halves, and that the target labels partition into output wires. Build the M_k, extract r = |A|, s = |B| and the term count. Search for a decomposition of rank m: start from the recursive Karatsuba schedule for (r, s) and then try to drop products greedily (a product t is droppable if the M_k are still in the span of the rest), verifying over F2 each time. Emit the match only if 7*m < 7*(current ccz/ccx count), i.e. only if m is strictly smaller; mult_4 has 16 terms over 4x4, so m = 9 (or 10-12 if a greedy drop stalls) and the match fires. Any circuit whose AND terms are not bilinear in two disjoint registers (adders, mcx) produces no match, which is a declared-precondition miss, not a rejection.
card.expected_effect: The 16 ccz gates (7 T each, 112 T total) are replaced by m Toffolis computing Karatsuba products, plus CNOTs (free in this cost model) and clean ancillas. At the Karatsuba optimum m = 9 the circuit costs 63 T; the conservative estimate, allowing that the greedy span check keeps one extra product per level or that the field-reduction wiring forces a 10th product, is m = 10, i.e. 70 T. That is below the best baseline (pyzx, 68) only at m = 9, and at m = 10 it lands just above it while still cutting the book's 112 by 42. Qubits rise 12 -> 18 (6 clean ancillas, all returned to |0>), CNOT count rises by roughly 40-60. No error is drawn, so the full 5e-4 rule pool and the whole synthesis half of the budget stay available for other circuits. This is not phase folding, not angle snapping and not a Toffoli-gadget substitution: it reduces the NUMBER of AND terms by the bilinear complexity of the map, which no baseline on this circuit exploits (pyzx reaches 68 by ZX-diagram phase merging on the 7-T decomposition, not by rediscovering Karatsuba), and it composes with any later per-Toffoli lowering.

Steinwandt, 'Quantum circuits for F_{2^n}-multiplication with subquadratic gate count', Quantum Information Processing 14 (2015) 2373-2386; D. J. Bernstein, 'Minimum number of bit operations for multiplication' (2009) for the rank-9 decomposition of 4x4 binary polynomial multiplication; M. Cenk and M. A. Hasan on Karatsuba variants over F2.

card.name: ccz_shared_pair_phase_polynomial_fusion
card.precondition: family dv_recon; Toffoli-level op list over x / cx / cz / z / t / tdg / ccx / ccz / h only (no rz, no measurement, no gadget), containing at least two ccz (or ccx, read as h-ccz-h on its target) and at least one cx, 6 <= qubits <= 34. Needs toffoli. Runs unitarily, no ancilla_room needed. A circuit with no ccz, or with fewer than two ccz inside any common Hadamard-free region, is excluded and costs nothing.
card.identity: Degree-3 phase-polynomial column merge. In a Hadamard-free region every ccz/cz/z/t is diagonal and therefore commutes with every other diagonal gate; only cx and x act linearly on the wires. So the region's action is: a GF(2)-affine map on the wires, times the diagonal phase exp(i*pi*f(x)) where f is a polynomial over GF(2)-affine parity labels, and `phasepoly.labels` gives each wire's label (mask, const) at every position. Read each ccz at position p on wires (u,v,w) as the cubic monomial P*Q*R where P,Q,R are the affine labels of u,v,w at p. The identity used is, for any three parities, (-1)^{PQR} * (-1)^{PQS} = (-1)^{PQ(R xor S)}, because the two exponents differ only when R=S=1, where their sum is even. Hence two ccz gates whose label triples agree on two slots, {P,Q,R} and {P,Q,S}, fuse into ONE ccz on (P, Q, R xor S): emit cx(c -> d) ; ccz(a, b, d) ; cx(c -> d) on representative wires a,b,c,d carrying P,Q,R,S (and, if R xor S is already the label of some live wire, even the two cx's are unnecessary). Two ccz become one ccz plus at most two cx: 14 T -> 7 T. The procedure does this globally rather than pairwise: for each maximal Hadamard-free region, collect the multiset of cubic monomials, cancel duplicates outright (P*Q*R twice = identity, 14 T -> 0 T), then greedily build a maximum matching on the graph whose vertices are the remaining monomials and whose edges join monomials sharing two labels, fusing each matched pair; repeat to fixpoint, since a fused monomial can share a pair with a third. Finally re-emit the region as (linear cx/x skeleton) + (one ccz per surviving cubic monomial, parities materialised by cx conjugation) + the region's original affine map restored.
card.correctness: Three independent exact arguments, all available inside the frozen API. (1) Algebraic: inside a Hadamard-free region the circuit is exactly (affine permutation) x (diagonal phase in the parity labels); the fusion identity above is an equality of GF(2) exponents, checked term by term, so the diagonal factor is unchanged as a function on all basis states, and the affine factor is restored because each conjugating cx is emitted in an undone pair. Global phase is untouched (all gates are real diagonal signs). (2) Proof-carrying: `phasepoly.witness(old_region_ops, new_region_ops, n)` is exactly a proof of equivalence for the Hadamard-free class in O(ops) with no matrices - the rewrite is only kept when the witness returns ok, so no application rests on my algebra. (3) Judge: both sides are Clifford+T (ccz lowers to 7 T), so the frozen verifier checks the changed window exactly over D[omega], and the whole-circuit pass re-checks against the ORIGINAL circuit. Hadamards are never crossed: regions come from `segments(ops, cut=('h',))` intersected with the wires each ccz touches, so no commutation through h is ever assumed. ccx is handled as h(target) ccz h(target), which is an exact rewrite, and the flanking h's are reabsorbed when the ccz re-emerges on the same target wire.
card.trigger: Fires once per maximal Hadamard-free region, at most once per region per pass. For each region: (1) run `phasepoly.labels` / `rotation_labels` over its ops to get the affine label of every wire at every position and the cubic monomial (as a sorted triple of label keys) of every ccz in it; (2) count monomials - emit a match if either (a) some monomial occurs an even number of times (free cancellation), or (b) at least one pair of distinct monomials shares two of its three labels; (3) the match carries the region bounds plus the chosen cancellation set and matching, computed deterministically (monomials ordered by label key, greedy matching in that order) so apply() is pure. Decline if the region has fewer than two ccz, or if no pair shares two labels, or if the re-emitted region does not price strictly lower, or if `witness` declines.

Each fused pair deletes one ccz = 7 T and adds at most 2 cx (cx is not priced before T in the lexicographic order). A greedy matching on 44 overlapping edges over 57 vertices realistically fuses ~20 pairs, and the uncompute half of the lookahead tree supplies outright duplicate monomials that cancel to 0 T. Estimate: 57 ccz -> ~37 ccz, 399 T -> ~259 T, with the h-count unchanged and the cx-count rising by at most ~40. The surviving ccz are the ones whose argument triples are pairwise disjoint, which is the genuine degree-3 content of the adder's phase polynomial - pyzx's full_reduce works on the ZX graph and does not perform this cubic-column merge, so the saving is not a repeat of the floor's pyzx-class rotation merging (which is degree-1 Pauli-axis merging and has zero headroom here), and it is unitary and exact, so it does not touch the ancilla_reconstruction lever that was already consumed.

card.name: jones_single_ccz_measured_four_t_lowering
card.precondition: dv_recon / Toffoli-level IRCircuit; needs toffoli (at least one ccz or ccx present), needs ancilla_room, measurement and classically controlled gates allowed; qubits <= 24. No rotations, no shared control pairs and no span condition required - every single ccz/ccx qualifies on its own.
card.identity: Lower EACH individual CCZ/CCX in isolation, not pairs. For a gate CCZ(x,y,z) (for CCX(x,y;z) the same with cz(a,z) replaced by cx(a,z)): take one fresh clean ancilla a in |0>, emit and_compute(x, y -> a) [Gidney's temporary-AND: 4 T, T-depth 1], then cz(a, z), then and_uncompute(a) [0 T: H on a, measure a, and on outcome 1 apply the classically controlled cz(x, y) fix-up, returning a to |0>]. Total 4 T per gate instead of the 7 T of the unitary Toffoli decomposition. The compute/uncompute brackets the gate immediately, so the ancilla's lifetime is three ops long: it is closed before the next match opens, ONE ancilla is reused by all 11 gates (qubits 14 -> 15), nothing about the surrounding op list is assumed, and no commutation analysis is needed. Matches are emitted one per ccz/ccx occurrence, in circuit order.
card.correctness: CCZ(x,y,z) is diagonal with eigenvalue (-1)^{xyz}; it therefore depends on x,y only through the Boolean product xy. If a carries xy then CZ(a,z) has eigenvalue (-1)^{(xy)z} = (-1)^{xyz} on every computational basis state, hence the two operators agree as operators and so on arbitrary superpositions (same for CCX, a permutation depending on x,y only through xy). Gidney's temporary-AND gadget (arXiv:1709.06648 Fig. 3, after Jones arXiv:1212.5069) prepares a = x AND y on a clean |0> ancilla using 4 T gates, exactly and unitarily. Its uncompute measures a in the X basis: the measurement collapses a but leaves a residual phase kickback (-1)^{m·xy} with m the outcome, which is removed exactly by the classically controlled CZ(x,y); after the fix-up the state is the original one on x,y,z with a back in |0>, for every branch and with the SAME branch coefficient for every input, so the branch-wise specification check (invariant 2: ancillas |0> -> |0>, phase consistency c_m independent of x) passes with Sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1. Error is exactly zero, so no budget is drawn. Jones' count is optimal-known for a single Toffoli with one ancilla and measurement: 4 T, versus 7 T for any unitary ancilla-free decomposition, which is why a purely unitary optimizer (pyzx at 47) cannot reach it.
card.trigger: Scan the op list once for gates with name in {ccz, ccx}. Emit one match per occurrence, carrying its position and its three wires, with the AND pair chosen as the two controls for ccx and, for ccz, as the two wires whose removal leaves the wire that is read least often nearby (any choice is correct; fix it deterministically as the two smallest wire indices for reproducibility). The only guards are: a clean ancilla is obtainable (append_ancillas / reuse of a closed one) and the gate has three distinct wires. There is no condition on neighbouring ops, so the trigger matches all 11 ccz of adder_6.
card.expected_effect: All 11 ccz of adder_6 drop from 7 T to 4 T each: 11*7 = 77 -> 11*4 = 44 T, i.e. -33 T (-42.9%), crossing the best baseline pyzx at 47 by 3 T. CNOT count rises by about 2 per gate and the qubit count by exactly 1 (14 -> 15) because the single ancilla is closed and reused after each gate; cost order is lexicographic in (T, qubits, CNOT), so the T drop decides. This is strictly per-gate and therefore immune to the failure mode of the span-sharing idea in history.json: no shared control pair, no 'controls unwritten over the span' hypothesis, nothing to invalidate. If some ccz are later also pair-shareable, that is an independent further win on top, but it is not assumed here.

card.precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz and ancilla_room; min_qubits 2, max_qubits 20. card.identity: For k commuting rotations of the SAME angle theta about Paulis P_1..P_k, prod_i exp(-i theta P_i / 2) depends only on the number of P_i that evaluate to -1. This is Hamming weight phasing; it is NOT phase folding (axes differ), NOT angle snapping (no angle is moved), and NOT a phase-gradient/constant-addition construction (no gradient catalyst register, no shared resource state, nothing amortized across the circuit - each angle class pays its own small adder tree and the rule is exact).
card.correctness: Each P_i is Hermitian with eigenvalues +-1 and the P_i pairwise commute, so they are simultaneously diagonalizable and the k exponentials may be slid to one common slice provided each P_i also commutes with every rotation Pauli strictly between the earliest and latest member (checked by the trigger) - Clifford ops between them are absorbed by the frame sweep, which is exact up to global phase. Parity copy: CNOTs from the support of P_i onto a clean ancilla a_i put x_i = P_i's eigenvalue bit on a_i, with the data unchanged; conjugating by it maps Z_{a_i} to P_i exactly, and the ladder is its own inverse. On the copies, prod_i exp(-i theta Z_{a_i}/2) = exp(-i(theta/2)(k - 2 HW(x))) = e^{-i theta k/2} * exp(i theta HW(x)); the global scalar is unobservable. With HW(x) = sum_j 2^j w_j, exp(i theta HW) = prod_j exp(i theta 2^j w_j) = prod_j Rz(-2^j theta) on w_j up to another global phase, because w_j is a computational-basis bit and the operator is diagonal. The full-adder tree computing HW is a reversible classical circuit, and Gidney's temporary-AND gadget is exact: its uncompute measures the target in the X basis and applies a classically controlled CZ, so on EVERY measurement branch the Kraus operator is the same unitary times the same scalar and the ancilla is returned to |0> deterministically (invariant 2 holds branch-wise, which is exactly what the judge's branch-wise specification check tests). Total error introduced: zero; the only error in the final circuit remains gridsynth's on the surviving rotations, which is cheaper than before because there are fewer of them.
card.trigger: Run pauli.frames(ops) to get Records (pos, theta, Pauli, on_grid). Drop records with on_grid. Normalize: replace (theta<0, P) by (|theta|, -P). Bucket by |theta| to 1e-9. For each bucket of size k >= 3, greedily take a maximal subset S that is pairwise commuting (pauli.commutes) and such that every member's Pauli commutes with the Pauli of every rotation record whose pos lies between min(pos in S) and max(pos in S). Let b = floor(log2 |S|) + 1 and let g = #{ j in [0,b) : 2^j * |theta| is a multiple of pi/4 (on_grid) }. Emit the match only if |S| - (b - g) >= 1, i.e. the number of off-grid rotations strictly falls; the match carries S, the common slice position (the position of the last member), the b weight bits and the |S| parity ancillas requested via append_ancillas. Emit one match per bucket, largest |S| first. On qft_8 this emits 4 matches: |S|=6 at pi/8 (b=3, weight angles pi/8, pi/4, pi/2 -> 1 off-grid, saves 5), |S|=5 at pi/16 (b=3 -> pi/16, pi/8, pi/4 -> 2 off-grid, saves 3), |S|=4 at pi/32 (b=3 -> 3 off-grid, saves 1), |S|=3 at pi/64 (b=2 -> 2 off-grid, saves 1); the pi/128 pair is correctly skipped by the net-reduction test.

card.name: global_budget_concentration_near_clifford_angle_snapping
card.precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz; 2 <= qubits <= 20. Requires at least one non-Clifford rz whose angle theta satisfies v4.api.angles.rz_distance(theta - nearest multiple of pi/4) <= the error the rule draws from the shared pool (5e-4), i.e. at least one angle within sin^-1(2*5e-4) of the pi/4 grid. On qae_13 the angle histogram contains the near-Clifford family -pi/2 + pi/2^k (-1.57002934, -1.56926235, -1.56772837, -1.5646604, -1.55852448, -1.54625263), whose first member is 7.67e-4 = pi/4096 away from -pi/2, so rz_distance = sin(3.83e-4) = 3.83e-4 < 5e-4 and the trigger matches there; circuits with no angle inside the whole pool are excluded and cost nothing.
card.identity: Rz(theta) = Rz(theta*) * Rz(theta - theta*) with theta* the nearest k*pi/4. If theta* is a multiple of pi/2 the factor Rz(theta*) is the Clifford z/s/sdg (0 T of synthesis), if it is an odd multiple of pi/4 it is t/tdg (1 T, no synthesis); the residual Rz(theta-theta*) is DROPPED and its phase-aligned operator distance |sin((theta-theta*)/2)| is charged to the ledger. The procedure is the allocator, not the snap: collect every rotation i of the whole circuit with cost_i = rz_distance(theta_i - theta_i*) and gain_i = the T that gridsynth stops paying for it (gain_i = T(eps_rz) if theta_i* is a pi/2 multiple, T(eps_rz) - 1 if it is an odd pi/4 multiple), sort by gain_i/cost_i, and greedily accept while sum of accepted cost_i <= the amount drawn, re-pricing after each accept because deleting one rotation lowers N_Rz and therefore RAISES eps_rz = eps_synth/N_Rz for every survivor, which lowers every survivor's cost by 3*log2(N_Rz/(N_Rz-1)) and can bring a second candidate inside the remaining pool. The whole 5e-4 pool is spent on the single globally best few rotations rather than divided between blocks.
card.correctness: Exact algebra: Rz is a one-parameter group, so the split Rz(theta) = Rz(theta*)Rz(theta-theta*) is an identity, and Rz(k*pi/2) in {z,s,sdg} and Rz(+-pi/4) in {t,tdg} are exactly representable (v4.api.dv.with_ops performs exactly this lowering). The only error is the deleted residual, a one-rotation window whose phase-aligned operator distance the judge measures as exactly |sin(delta/2)| = v4.api.angles.rz_distance(delta); distances of independent accepted snaps add in the worst case (diagonal phase errors on independent basis bits do not cancel in the operator norm, so the sum is the honest bound and is what is drawn). No qubits, no measurement, no Clifford frame change beyond a diagonal gate replacing a diagonal gate, so commutation with everything downstream is unchanged and the whole-circuit check against the ORIGINAL circuit sees only the drawn error. Each accepted application is individually verified, so a mis-priced candidate is rejected, not silently kept.
card.trigger: Over the op list after the book: for every op with v4.api.dv.is_rotation and not v4.api.dv.on_grid(angle), compute theta* = the nearest multiple of pi/4 (v4.api.angles.dyadic(theta, 2)) and cost = v4.api.angles.rz_distance(theta - theta*). Emit matches only for rotations with cost <= v4.api.budget.remaining(), ordered by (T saved)/cost descending; emit them one at a time so the runner prices and verifies each before the next is offered, and stop when budget.draw(cost) refuses. Rotations already on the pi/4 grid, and rotations whose distance exceeds the pool, are not matched.
card.expected_effect: On qae_13 exactly one rotation is affordable: the angle -1.57002934 = -pi/2 + pi/4096 snaps to -pi/2 = sdg for 3.83e-4 of the pool, turning one of the 88 synthesized rotations into a free Clifford. That removes its gridsynth sequence (~51 T at eps_rz = 1.136e-5, from (4526 - 14 explicit T)/88 = 51.3 T per rotation) and drops N_Rz from 88 to 87, which raises eps_rz for the 87 survivors and shaves 3*log2(88/87) = 0.05 T off each, ~4 T more. Second-order: with eps_rz relaxed, no further angle comes inside the 1.17e-4 left, so the allocator stops. The point of difference against the floor's DPF rule is allocation, not snapping: DPF splits the 5e-4 into equal per-block shares over ~20 width-4 blocks, giving each block ~2.5e-5 - an order of magnitude less than the 3.83e-4 this one snap needs - so DPF provably cannot buy it (fingerprint fixable_at_k['2'] = 0 at the per-rotation eps_rz threshold, but 76 at k=14, i.e. the circuit has exactly one angle that a concentrated budget can move onto the pi/4 grid). Expected final T ~4471, inside the 151 T of angle_cost headroom and honestly short of DPF's 4264.
card.source: Ross & Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations' (arXiv:1403.2975) for the 3*log2(1/eps) cost law that makes gain/cost the right greedy key; Gheorghiu, Mosca & Mukhopadhyay, 'T-count and T-depth of any multi-qubit unitary' / Kliuchnikov-Maslov-Mosca on exact pi/4-multiple representability; the non-uniform precision-allocation argument of Campbell, 'Shorter gate sequences by mixing unitaries' (PRA 95, 042306) and of Bocharov-Roetteler-Svore on budgeting synthesis error across many rotations rather than splitting it uniformly.

card.name: toffoli_uncompute_measurement_elision
card.precondition: family = dv_recon (Toffoli-level IRCircuit, zero continuous Rz, measurement-free input); needs toffoli and hadamard; 3 <= qubits <= 20 so the whole-circuit judge still runs; the op list must contain at least two ccz/ccx ops sharing an unordered control pair; no extra qubits are requested (resource use is a mid-circuit measurement on an EXISTING wire, so ancilla_room is not required). The rule only ever edits the LATER member of a compute/uncompute pair; circuits with no such pair are declined before any rewrite and cost nothing.
card.identity: Recognise AND-scratch pairs and delete the uncomputation, keeping the computation untouched. Read every H-sandwiched CCZ as a Toffoli: h(t) ccz(a,b,t) h(t) == ccx(a,b -> t). Let G1 = ccx(a,b -> t) at position i and G2 = ccx(a,b -> t) at position j > i be two Toffolis with the SAME unordered control pair {a,b} and the SAME target t, such that (i) t is certified to be in |0> immediately before G1, (ii) no op strictly between i and j writes t (no x/cx/ccx/ccz-with-H targeting t, no h on t) -- t may be READ freely, i.e. appear as a control of cx/ccx/ccz or be acted on by diagonal gates, and (iii) no op strictly between i and j writes a or b (a, b may be read). Then t holds exactly a AND b on the whole span, and G2 is a pure uncomputation. REWRITE: delete G2 (together with its two sandwiching h(t) if it is encoded as h-ccz-h) and emit in its place the measurement-based uncompute, which `v4.api.dv` exposes natively as the 0-T gadget `and_uncompute(a, b, t)`: h(t); measure t -> m; classically controlled cz(a,b) on m = 1; the wire t is thereafter a fresh |0> scratch wire (it is NOT removed, so the qubit count is unchanged). The computing Toffoli G1 is left exactly as it is -- this rule does not re-synthesise it, does not introduce `and_compute`, and does not change any CCZ that is not the second half of such a pair. A maximal chain ccx(a,b->t) ... ccx(a,b->t) ... ccx(a,b->t) with the same {a,b},t is treated as consecutive pairs, the even-indexed members being uncomputations.
card.correctness: Under conditions (i)-(iii) a forward GF(2) argument gives the state of t on the span exactly: t = 0 before G1, G1 sets t ^= a*b, and nothing between i and j writes t, a or b, so just before G2 the register is in a superposition of basis states sum_x alpha_x |a(x), b(x), rest(x)> |t = a(x) AND b(x)>, i.e. t is a deterministic function of the surviving data and carries no independent amplitude. G2 would map t back to 0. The gadget does the same thing up to a Pauli correction: H on t followed by a computational-basis measurement is an X-basis measurement, whose outcome m in {0,1} is uniform and INDEPENDENT of x because <+|a&b> = <-|a&b>^(+-) has modulus 1/sqrt(2) for both values of a&b; the post-measurement data state is (-1)^{m*(a(x) AND b(x))} alpha_x |data(x)>, i.e. the residual operator is CZ(a,b)^m, which the classically controlled cz(a,b) undoes exactly. Hence each branch applies K_m = U_correct with c_m = 1/sqrt(2) -- the SAME constant for every input x, so invariant 2 (phase consistency) holds, and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1. The wire t is left in a product state |0> or |1> that the gadget resets, so it re-enters the circuit as clean |0> scratch exactly as after G2: the branch-wise specification check the judge runs on measured constructions is satisfied with zero ledger charge, and the removed Toffoli's 7 T are replaced by Clifford + classical control only. The h-ccz-h == ccx reading is the exact CCX = H_t CCZ H_t identity over Z[omega]; a ccz whose target is not H-sandwiched is never matched. Certification of (i): forward symbolic ANF propagation (wire -> set of GF(2) monomials) from the circuit's declared initial state, with the input register left symbolic and scratch wires initialised to the constant 0; the wire must still carry the constant 0 at position i. If the analysis cannot prove t = 0, the match is not emitted -- no guessing, so a wrong ancilla guess can never be the reason for a rejection.
card.trigger: One forward pass. (1) Fold h(q) ccz(a,b,q) h(q) patterns, with no other op touching q in between, into virtual ccx(a,b -> q) entries, remembering the three original op indices. (2) Propagate per-wire ANF (frozenset of int bitmasks, constant 1 = empty mask) under x: p ^= 1, cx: p_b ^= p_a, ccx: p_t ^= p_a * p_b, cutting at any h that was not folded (such an h makes its wire's ANF unknown and poisons that wire until it is overwritten). (3) For each virtual ccx at position i with p_t == {} (the constant 0) just before it, scan forward for the next virtual ccx with the same unordered {a,b} and the same t; accept it as a match iff every op strictly between the two has t, a, b outside its TARGET set (controls are fine) and no unfolded h touches t, a or b in the span. (4) Emit one match per such pair: (i, j, a, b, t, the op indices to delete). Matches are emitted in circuit order, disjoint in j, and the pass is re-run after each accepted application so that a newly cleaned scratch wire can start a new pair. apply() splices out G2's ops and inserts `and_uncompute(a, b, t)`; the qubit count and every other op are unchanged.
card.expected_effect: modred_21's entire non-Clifford content is the 17 ccz (119 T = 17 x 7); the 30 h, 24 x and 3 cx are free. The 'h ccz h' trigram (11x) says most ccz are H-sandwiched Toffolis, and the fingerprint's 7 shared_control_pairs says control pairs are reused. Modular reduction against a constant computes a comparison out of AND terms on scratch wires, conditionally subtracts, and then UNCOMPUTES the comparison, so the circuit should contain a handful of exact compute/uncompute Toffoli pairs on the same control pair and target. Each pair that fires deletes one Toffoli = 7 T and adds only h, a measurement and one classically controlled cz. Conservatively 2 pairs survive the strict same-controls / no-intervening-write guard: 119 -> 105 T, with upside to 119 - 28 = 91 if 4 fire. Qubits stay at 11, CNOT count is unchanged (the classically controlled cz is not a two-qubit quantum gate on the critical cost order's CNOT tally only if priced as such; otherwise it adds at most one cz per fired pair), zero error drawn. Distinct from the prefiltered temporary-AND card: that one re-synthesised EVERY ccz into a 4-T and_compute (+1 ancilla, saving 3 T on all 17); this one adds no ancilla, leaves every computing Toffoli alone, and takes 7 T only where a Toffoli is provably redundant uncomputation.
card.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018), arXiv:1709.06648 (measurement-based uncomputation of an AND: X-basis measurement plus a classically controlled CZ, 0 T); the recognition of uncomputation Toffolis on |0>-initialised scratch wires by GF(2)/ANF propagation is the standard reversible-logic pebbling argument (Bennett 1973; Soeken-Chattopadhyay DAC 2016), and the same elision is used throughout Gidney-Ekera, arXiv:1905.09749.

card.name: cubic_signature_tensor_todd_reduction
card.precondition: Toffoli-level IRCircuit (family dv_recon), measurement-free, gate names drawn only from {ccz, ccx, cx, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, h}, at least 4 ccz/ccx gates, and at least one Hadamard-free op range containing >= 2 ccz/ccx gates (api.dv.segments(ops, cut=('h',)) must return such a range). 4 <= qubits <= 20. No ancillas, no measurement, no continuous rotations. Circuits with Rz rotations (qft/qpe/hhl/qae/tfim) and circuits whose Toffolis are all isolated between Hadamards produce no match and cost nothing.
card.identity: TODD / Reed-Muller reduction of the CUBIC PHASE POLYNOMIAL, not of rotations. Take each Hadamard-free segment; it is a diagonal unitary U_f, f: F2^n -> Z8, since cx/x are linear and ccz/t are diagonal. Push the linear maps to the front with api.phasepoly.labels, so each ccz(p,q,r) contributes the degree-3 monomial l_p l_q l_r and each t/tdg contributes a degree-1 term, over the affine parity labels l. Represent f canonically by its SIGNATURE MATRIX S in F2^{n x m}: f(x) = sum_{l=1..m} (pi/4) * <s_l, x> with all coefficients odd, so the segment's T-count is exactly m (the number of columns). Expanding each ccz by 8*xyz = (x)+(y)+(z)-(x^y)-(y^z)-(x^z)+(x^y^z) gives the initial S with 7 columns per ccz, then equal columns are merged (two equal odd columns sum to a Clifford S gate). Then iterate the duplicate-and-destroy move: for every ordered pair of columns (a, b), set z = s_a AND s_b (entrywise product over F2) and update every column by s_l -> s_l XOR (<s_l-dependent parity> * z) in the way that leaves the symmetric third-order tensor T_{ijk} = sum_l s_{l,i} s_{l,j} s_{l,k} (and the lower-order data) invariant; after the update columns a and b coincide, and a duplicated pair is destroyed because T^2 = S is Clifford. Each successful move lowers m by 2 and emits one tracked Clifford correction (S/Z/CZ) that is appended to the segment's Clifford skeleton. Run moves greedily to a fixed point; then, as the second stage, do the Amy-Mosca refinement: the set of all signature matrices with the same tensor is a coset of the punctured Reed-Muller code RM(n-4, n)*, so search that coset locally (random walks of low-weight code additions, keeping the best) for a representative of smaller Hamming weight, i.e. fewer odd columns. Finally re-emit the segment as cx/t/tdg over the recovered parities (a CNOT network per column, synthesized by Gaussian elimination on the parity set) followed by the accumulated Clifford.
card.correctness: A Hadamard-free Clifford+T+CCZ circuit is a linear reversible map composed with a diagonal unitary U_f, and U_f is determined exactly by the Z8-valued polynomial f, hence by its coefficients of degree 1, 2 and 3 taken mod 8, mod 4 and mod 2 respectively. The degree-3 part mod 2 is precisely the symmetric tensor T_{ijk} built from the signature matrix; two signature matrices with the same T (and the same lower-order data after the recorded Clifford fix-ups) define the SAME diagonal unitary up to Clifford, which is why the duplicate-and-destroy update is an exact identity and not an approximation: it is verified column-algebraically over F2 before emission, and the emitted Clifford correction accounts for every term that changed modulus class. Destroying a duplicated pair uses T(p) T(p) = S(p), exact. The coset statement is the standard one: f's degree-<=3 representations differ exactly by elements of the punctured Reed-Muller code, so every coset element yields the same unitary; minimizing Hamming weight in the coset is minimizing T-count, and any candidate is re-checked by recomputing the tensor. Equivalence of the rewritten segment is further proved in O(ops) by api.phasepoly.witness (the Hadamard-free class is exactly where that witness is valid), and the judge then certifies the changed window exactly in D[omega], both sides being Clifford+T. Zero error is drawn: error_class exact, no ledger charge, no ancillas, no measurement, same qubit count.
card.trigger: One match per Hadamard-free segment returned by api.dv.segments(ops, cut=('h',)) that contains >= 2 ccz/ccx gates (gf2^4_mult has long ccz runs: the trigram 'ccz ccz ccz' occurs 4 times and only 14 Hadamards serve 16 ccz, so adjacent Toffolis sharing a target leave their conjugating Hadamards cancelled and the runs are long). Build S for the segment, run TODD to a fixed point and then the RM coset walk with a fixed seed and a fixed iteration cap (deterministic). Emit the match only if the final column count m_new is strictly less than the segment's current T-count and the re-emitted CNOT network does not raise the lexicographic cost; otherwise emit nothing for that segment. Segments with a single ccz cannot reduce (no pair of columns to duplicate) and are skipped, which is a trigger miss, not a rejection.
card.expected_effect: The 16 ccz gates currently cost 7 T each (112 T). Fusing the expanded signature columns inside each Hadamard-free run already collapses the shared parities between Toffolis that act on overlapping label sets, and the TODD moves then remove T gates in pairs; the RM coset walk picks up what TODD's greedy fixed point leaves. This is the mechanism that is documented to take GF(2^4)-mult from 112 T to 68 T (Tpar/TODD) and below it with Reed-Muller coset decoding. Because our segments are cut by the 14 Hadamards, the cross-segment merges that a global gadgetized treatment would get are not available, so I estimate landing near 64 T rather than the best published number: 112 -> ~64, i.e. 48 T removed, beating pyzx's 68. Conservative floor if the coset walk adds nothing beyond the greedy fixed point in the cut segments: ~76 T (36 saved). Qubits stay 12; CNOT count rises by roughly 30-60 from re-synthesizing the parity networks, which is only the third lexicographic key. Not a repeat of the floor: the floor merges first-order rotations as Pauli exponentials (degree-1 phase gadgets) and never touches the degree-3 part of the phase polynomial, which is where every T in this circuit lives.
card.source: L. E. Heyfron and E. T. Campbell, 'An efficient quantum compiler that reduces T count', Quantum Sci. Technol. 4, 015004 (2019) [TODD/TOOL, arXiv:1712.01557]; M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits via matroid partitioning' (Tpar, 2014); M. Amy and M. Mosca, 'T-count optimization and Reed-Muller codes', IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 65 (2019) [arXiv:1601.07363].

card.name: temporary_and_pair_gadget_substitution
card.precondition: family dv_recon; Toffoli-level op list over x / cx / cz / z / h / ccx / ccz only (no rz, no off-grid rotation, no pre-existing measurement), containing at least one ccz or ccx, 6 <= qubits <= 34, ancilla_room not required (the gadget reuses the wire that the Toffoli already writes). A circuit with no ccz/ccx, or in which no ccz/ccx target can be certified |0> immediately before it, is excluded by the declared precondition and costs nothing.
card.identity: LOCAL, per-Toffoli substitution of Gidney's temporary AND - no whole-circuit semantic recognition, which is what distinguishes it from attempt 1's global adder resynthesis. Step 0 (normalisation only, no cost change): a pattern h(t) ; ccz(a,b,t) ; h(t) with no other gate touching t between the h's is rewritten to ccx(a,b -> t); this is an exact identity because H Z H = X on the controlled branch. Step 1 (compute): if the target t of a ccx(a,b -> t) is certified to be in |0> immediately before it, replace that ccx by and_compute(a,b -> t), Gidney's 4-T temporary-AND gadget (4 T, 0 extra qubits, t holds a AND b exactly). Cost 7 T -> 4 T. Step 2 (uncompute, the large half): if additionally there is a LATER ccx(a,b -> t) on the SAME ordered wire triple such that between the two occurrences t is touched only as a CONTROL of cx/cz/ccz (never a target, never under h, never measured), replace that later ccx by and_uncompute(t): measure t in the X basis and apply the classically controlled cz(a,b) fix-up. Cost 7 T -> 0 T. A matched pair therefore goes 14 T -> 4 T, a saving of 10 T per pair; an unpaired compute on a clean target goes 14 T -> ... 7 T -> 4 T, a saving of 3 T. Controls a,b are untouched by the rewrite, so the gadget is a strictly local window replacement and the rest of the op list is re-emitted verbatim.
card.correctness: Three parts. (1) Zero-certification of t: a conservative forward |0>-analysis over the op list - t is |0> at position p if, on every gate before p that touches t, either t is untouched, or t is the target of a cx/ccx whose controls are themselves certified |0>, or t was restored by an earlier and_uncompute / matched ccx pair. Only wires the analysis proves |0> are rewritten; anything unproven declines. This is the ONLY premise the rewrite needs, because CCX acting on a |0> target is exactly the AND map |a,b,0> -> |a,b,ab>, and and_compute implements precisely that map on a |0> target (Gidney 2018, Fig. 3: 4 T gates, exact, no approximation and no error budget). (2) The uncompute is exact branch-wise: between compute and uncompute, t appears only as a control of diagonal/classical gates, so the joint state is sum_x alpha_x |x> |ab(x)> with no superposition structure in t beyond the computed value; measuring t in the X basis yields outcome m in {+,-} with equal weight, the data is unchanged for m = +, and for m = - it differs by exactly the phase (-1)^{a b}, which the classically controlled cz(a,b) fix-up cancels identically. So K_m |x> = c_m |f(x)> with the same c_m = 1/sqrt(2) for every input x and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1 - invariant 2 holds branch-wise, which is why the rule is exact, error_budget 0, and does not draw on the 5e-4 pool. (3) Judge-side: the compute half is a unitary Clifford+T window and is checked exactly over D[omega]; the measured half is checked by the relaxed-window branch agreement (both measurement branches must agree with the original ccx on the data wires with t returned to |0>), i.e. the rule never asserts its own correctness.
card.trigger: Fires once per certified Toffoli, scanning the op list in order. (1) Normalise h-ccz-h sandwiches to ccx (and record the inverse so untouched ones are re-emitted unchanged). (2) Run the |0>-analysis above, producing the set Z of (position, target) pairs where the target is certified |0>. (3) For each such ccx at position i on (a,b -> t), search forward for the first ccx on the same ordered triple (a,b -> t) at position j > i, and check the between-window condition: no gate in (i, j) has t as a target, applies h to t, or measures t, and a and b are not written between i and j (if either control is written, decline that pair - the fix-up cz(a,b) would act on the wrong parity). If all hold, emit one match {i, j, a, b, t} for the pair; if no partner exists, emit a compute-only match {i, a, b, t}. (4) Matches are disjoint by construction (a position belongs to at most one match, taken greedily in index order), so apply() is pure and deterministic. Decline if Z is empty, if the rewritten circuit does not price strictly lower, or if any emitted window fails the judge.

card.name: ccz_phase_polynomial_parity_merge_todd
card.precondition: dv_recon / Toffoli-level IRCircuit with at least two ccz/ccx gates and no non-Clifford rz (rotations == 0): the non-Clifford content is entirely hidden inside ccz/ccx, so the book's rotation-frame rules see nothing to merge (fingerprint: rotations 0, foldable 0). Needs toffoli, hadamard allowed, measurement_free, no ancilla_room needed, qubits <= 20.
card.identity: Do NOT lower each ccz on its own. Instead expose each ccz as its phase polynomial over F2 parities and merge across gates. (1) Cut the op list at Hadamards into maximal {cx, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, cz, ccz}-segments (api.dv.segments / api.phasepoly.labels gives each wire's affine parity label (mask, const) inside a segment). (2) Inside a segment, replace every ccz(a,b,c) by its exact diagonal expansion as a sum over parities: CCZ = exp(i pi/4 * [p_a + p_b + p_c - p_{a^b} - p_{b^c} - p_{a^c} + p_{a^b^c}]) where p_S is the parity of the label masks of the involved wires, i.e. seven Rz(+-pi/4) gates on the parities {a}, {b}, {c}, {a^b}, {b^c}, {a^c}, {a^b^c}; cz(a,b) is likewise exp(i pi/2 * [...]) over {a},{b},{a^b} and contributes only Clifford (pi/2) weight. (3) Accumulate the whole segment as a single phase polynomial: a map from parity mask (plus affine constant sign) to an angle coefficient mod 2pi, adding coefficients of EQUAL parities. Every pair of equal parities with opposite pi/4 sign annihilates (T * Tdg = I), every pair with equal sign fuses into a Clifford S (pi/2) which costs 0 T, and 8 copies vanish. (4) Re-emit: each surviving coefficient that is an odd multiple of pi/4 becomes one T/Tdg conjugated by a CNOT ladder that builds its parity and unbuilds it; coefficients that are multiples of pi/2 become S/Z (free). (5) Before re-emission, apply one round of TODD/third-order-duplicate reduction (Heyfron-Campbell) on the F2 signature matrix of the odd (T-paying) terms: search pairs of columns a,b whose symmetric difference, when added as the F2 vector a+b to every column, reduces the number of odd-weight columns; each successful move removes 2 T. Iterate to a fixed point, deterministically (lexicographic pair order, first improving move). Re-emit the CNOT ladder from the reduced signature matrix. The rewrite is one segment at a time, so the judge prices and verifies each segment replacement independently.
card.correctness: A Hadamard-free Clifford+T+CCZ circuit on n wires acts as |x> -> e^{i f(A x + c)} |B x + d> with B, A over F2 and f a sum of linear-parity phase terms; this is the standard phase-polynomial normal form (Amy-Maslov-Mosca). The CCZ identity used in (2) is the exact Reed-Muller expansion of the Boolean function x1 x2 x3 as an F2-parity sum: x1 x2 x3 = (x1 + x2 + x3 - (x1^x2) - (x2^x3) - (x1^x3) + (x1^x2^x3))/4 over the integers, hence CCZ = exp(i pi x1 x2 x3) = exp(i pi/4 [sum of the seven signed parities]); each factor is a diagonal Rz on a parity, so all factors commute and the product is order-independent. Equal parities therefore add their angles exactly, with no approximation and no commutation hypothesis beyond staying inside one Hadamard-free segment (where the parity labels are constant functions of the segment input). T * Tdg = I and T^2 = S are exact, so every cancellation and fusion is exact; re-emitting a parity by a CNOT ladder and unbuilding it restores the linear part B exactly, and the leftover linear map is fixed up by the CNOTs already recorded in labels(). TODD's move adds the F2 vector a+b to all columns of the signature matrix; Heyfron-Campbell prove this leaves the induced cubic form (hence the unitary) invariant up to Clifford corrections that are tracked and reapplied, so it is an exact T-count reduction. Everything is Clifford+T on both sides, so the judge's exact D[omega] check on the changed window decides, and no error budget is drawn. Why this is not the floor's phase-gadget fusion: the floor's pauli_frame_rotation_merge / pauli_exponential_commutation_merge operate on ROTATION ops present in the op list, and this circuit has zero rotations - 100% of its 77 T sit inside 11 opaque ccz gates. The content here is the F2-linear/Reed-Muller algebra that only appears once the ccz are expanded, which no rule in the book does; in the ripple-carry adder the compute and uncompute carry Toffolis generate the SAME parities (the carry wire's label is unchanged between them), so their pi/4 terms cancel pairwise instead of each paying 7 T.
card.trigger: Scan the op list. Fire on each maximal Hadamard-free segment (cut set {h, measure}) that contains >= 2 gates from {ccz, ccx} (ccx(a,b;c) is handled as h(c) ccz(a,b,c) h(c), i.e. its target Hadamards become new segment cuts and are left in place, so only the ccz core enters the polynomial). Guards: the segment's gates are all in {x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, cx, cz, ccz}; no measurement or classically controlled gate inside; segment touches <= 20 wires. Emit one match per qualifying segment, largest ccz-count first, carrying the segment index range. On adder_6 the 'h ccz h' trigram occurs 11 times and 'cx h ccz' 9 times, so the ccx targets' Hadamards split the circuit; the match set is the segments between them, and after the first merge pass the surviving T-ladders themselves open longer Hadamard-free runs, so the rule is re-triggered to a fixed point.
card.expected_effect: The 11 ccz expand into 77 signed pi/4 parity terms. In a ripple-carry adder every carry Toffoli is mirrored by an uncompute Toffoli on the same three wires with the same parity labels, and the fingerprint already reports 5 shared_control_pairs; those produce equal parities with opposite effective sign across the pair, so their pi/4 terms either cancel outright or fuse to Clifford S. Counting conservatively: the 5 mirrored pairs contribute ~10 cancelling parity classes out of their 70 terms, and the TODD pass removes a further 2 T per successful column move.
